title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: The continuous-batcher scheduler currently optimizes throughput by aggregating requests into multi-request batches. Under skewed workloads (heavy hot-model traffic mixed with low-priority/background traffic) we observed queueing unfairness and request starvation that drove high tail queue_wait and a non-trivial number of requests hitting internal timeouts. Motivation: Reduce starvation for low-priority requests without degrading overall throughput, provide configurable soft/hard timeouts to surface latency trade-offs, and add observability to monitor fairness violations. This PR implements a set of scheduler-level changes and configuration knobs: (1) per-slot aging score (exponentially-weighted) to increase scheduling priority for requests that have waited longer, (2) token-based fairness counters scoped per-model-and-priority to prevent a single hot customer from monopolizing a slot for long-running sequences, (3) bounded per-slot queue depth with overflow routing (fast-path fallback to a small-context variant when configured), (4) soft_timeout_ms and hard_timeout_ms support where soft timeouts trigger best-effort fallbacks instead of hard cancellation, and (5) new metrics and tracing spans to detect fairness violations and starvation events. Key design decisions: - Aging window and fairness tokens are tunable via the scheduler config (defaults chosen conservatively to avoid throughput regressions). - Soft-timeout fallback is opt-in and requires a compatible model variant; fallback routing is a best-effort downgrade to preserve availability. - Limits (max_queue_depth_per_slot) use a per-slot admission control to bound queue growth and keep tail latency predictable. Files changed (high level): runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler.go (core changes), runtime/continuous_batcher/queue.go (bounded queueing + overflow), runtime/continuous_batcher/config.go (new knobs), runtime/continuous_batcher/metrics.go (new metrics), runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler_test.go (unit tests), integration/perf/continuous_batcher_fairness_test.go (integration/perf test), redwood-docs/guides/continuous-batcher-tuning.md (doc), perf-canary/jobs/continuous-batcher-fairness.yml (perf job), observability-pack/dashboards/scheduler-fairness.json (dashboard), CI config updates for perf job. Testing and results: Added deterministic unit tests for aging and token counters and an integration perf harness simulating skewed workloads. Perf-canary runs on a 4-GPU test cluster show: 95th percentile queue_wait reduced by ~32% and end-to-end 95th percentile token latency improved by ~18% under simulated hot-model skew; under uniform workloads throughput impact is <2%. Observability: added metrics scheduler.queue_wait_ms, scheduler.starved_requests, scheduler.fairness_violation_count, scheduler.soft_timeout_fallback_count and tracing spans scheduler.enqueue and scheduler.dequeue. Rollout: default behavior unchanged unless admin toggles new scheduler flags; recommended gradual rollout via feature flag and perf-canary monitoring. Backward compatibility / migration: No breaking API changes. New flags are optional. Customers using Dedicated/Private should evaluate fallback behavior when enabling soft_timeouts. See redwood-docs/guides/continuous-batcher-tuning.md for tuning guidance and knob recommendations.

review_comments: Lena Huang (reviewer): Could you make the fairness window configurable per-tenant? In some enterprise tests we want different aggression levels.
Asha Patel (author): Added per-tenant override in config.go and documented example in the tuning guide. Kept sane global default to avoid perf regressions.
Connor McBride (reviewer): The soft-timeout fallback looks useful but we need a clear failure mode. What happens if fallback preparation fails?

Asha Patel (author): Fallback is best-effort; if fallback preparation fails we fall back to the existing overflow path (reject or queue depending on policy) and emit scheduler.soft_timeout_fallback_failure metric. Updated code and tests to cover this.
Rohit Sharma (reviewer): There's a potential lock-holder path in dequeue that could regress throughput under extreme concurrency. Please add a microbenchmark.
Asha Patel (author): Added lock contention microbenchmark and refactored dequeue to reduce critical section. Benchmarks show <2% throughput delta on uniform workloads.
Connor McBride (reviewer): CI flaky on perf job in first run; re-ran and all checks passed.
Lena Huang (approver): Approve after documentation and perf-canary green.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and starvation prevention: adds aging-based priority, per-model token fairness, bounded per-slot queues with overflow/fallback routing, and configurable soft/hard timeouts. Observability improvements: scheduler.queue_wait_ms, scheduler.starved_requests, scheduler.fairness_violation_count, scheduler.soft_timeout_fallback_count. Default behavior remains stable; operators can enable soft-timeout fallbacks and per-tenant fairness overrides. See docs/guides/continuous-batcher-tuning.md for tuning guidance.
